doc.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017

title: Blindfold test: King Oliver's 'Sobbin' Blues'
summary: Pelote identifies King Oliver's band and recalls Armstrong being placed at the back to balance the recording.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Okay, you recall the Down Beat blindfold tests?
Okay, so I’m going to give you one.
Uh oh. Here’s where my expertise goes down the toilet. Ed used to do this to me all the time. He’d go pick some record and it was like —
It sounds like King Oliver’s band.
I love to picture — I wish I could have been a fly on the wall, I picture them in that studio playing in that megaphone and stuff.

Oh, I would love to see that too. God. Because from what I heard and read, Armstrong was so powerful that they had to put him in the back of the room. Really. Oliver was in the front and he was back — it’s the only way they could balance it. Really. It must have been wild.
